facts.claim: Klear-AgentForge-8B is reported at 39.4 SWE-bench Verified and 33.8 Aider-Polyglot (paper Table 3; README coding table). The README note says Verified was evaluated with mini-swe-agent-plus.
Sec. 3.1: Verified is the 500-issue human-validated subset, run with the mini-swe-agent-plus scaffold with each run capped at 200 steps and 64k context.

For SWE the paper states no temperature, top_p, per-turn max tokens, thinking mode, number of runs or seeds, serving engine or scoring harness. The text never mentions 'seed', 'pass@1', vLLM or SGLang. Other benchmarks do get settings: BFCL T=0.7/top_p 0.95/16k; tau-bench T=0.8 reported as avg@4; Aider T=0.7/top_p 0.8/24K. Researcher 3's '39.4 (pass@1, single run)' label is not supported by the paper: single-run is plausible but unstated.
The arXiv listing shows only v1, submitted Sat 8 Nov 2025 (764 KB), 20 pages, 7 figures.
Merging lowered coding scores: Verified 40.4 -> 39.4 and Aider 35.1 -> 33.8 (Sec. 3.4.3). Joint multi-task RL (tool use + SWE, 3:1 step schedule) gave BFCL v3 70.8 and Verified 39.6.

Paper Table 4 gives Klear-AgentForge-8B-SFT 38.2 on Verified (tau Retail 54.8, Airline 32.0) and 32B-SFT 55.2. The mini-swe-agent-plus README instead lists Klear-Agent-8B-SFT 39.0, 8B-RL 40.4, 32B-SFT 55.2 and 32B-RL 61.4. The dataset card also shows 39.0, next to a badge linking Klear-AgentForge-8B-SFT, and the HF 'mini-swe-agent-plus' collection pairs the dataset with that model. Whether 38.2 and 39.0 describe the same checkpoint is unresolved.
With 1-8 sampled candidates on Verified, Agent Confidence Select reaches 0.452 at N=8. The single-sample value appears only in Fig. 7b.

No OpenHands, SWE-agent or other-scaffold SWE number exists for the 8B model. Table 1 covers Claude only: Sonnet 4 gets 70.4 on OpenHands, 66.6 on SWE-agent, 64.9 on mini-swe-agent (79.1 turns) and 67.0 on the plus fork (67.3 turns); Sonnet 4.5 gets 70.6 vs 71.8. For Claude 3.7 on SWE-agent the paper says 62.4 but the scaffold README says 58.2.

Table 3: Qwen3-8B Thinking 9.8* and Non-Thinking 8.0*, and Qwen3-30A3B-2507-Instruct 17.6*; the asterisk means the authors' own eval script. Qwen3-Coder-30A3B-Instruct 51.6 has no asterisk, so it comes from an official report; the paper does not say which scaffold.

MIT-licensed GitHub fork of SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent with __version__ 1.14.4. The first fork commit, 0a6ef3e0 (2025-10-22, message 'start'), has parent upstream eeaf79b4 (2025-10-21); the fork is 10 commits ahead and 0 behind that base. Latest commit 3dfa5e26 (2026-01-20) is README-only.

Actions are plain text, not function calling. agents/default.py extracts actions with regex ```bash\s*\n(.*?)\n``` and raises FormatError unless there is exactly one match. The config has no tools key, and litellm.completion receives only messages plus config model_kwargs. The paper says the scaffold does not rely on model-side tool-calling interfaces.

At environment init, `docker cp` copies environments/str_replace.py (169 lines, stdlib only) into the container as /testbed/edit_via_str_replace. It replaces only a unique match; exit 2 = not found, 3 = multiple matches, 1 = other error. A del_edit_tool() method exists, but no call to it was found in agents/default.py or run/extra/swebench_pool_way.py. So `git add -A` at submit may include the helper file in the patch (inference).

swebench_add_edit_tool.yaml sets step_limit 200, cost_limit 3, cwd /testbed and a 60 s command timeout. Its model is claude-sonnet-4-20250514 at temperature 1.0 with drop_params, with no max_tokens and no tools. The prompt has a 5-step recommended workflow, forbids modifying tests and config files, and uses <returncode>/<output> observations. This is a Claude config, not a documented 8B setting.

The prompt instructs `echo MINI_SWE_AGENT_FINAL_OUTPUT && git add -A && git diff --cached`. The agent accepts either MINI_SWE_AGENT_FINAL_OUTPUT or COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT as the first output line, with no returncode check.

swebench_pool_way.py maps 'verified' to princeton-nlp/SWE-Bench_Verified and uses swebench/sweb.eval.x86_64.* images. It writes only preds.json and trajectories and has no retry or multi-attempt logic; scoring is undocumented. It also accepts undocumented local-JSON subsets 'verified100', 'verified236' and 'mysmith', which suggests internal Verified subsets (purpose unknown).

When the local_vllm_server_ips_filename env var is set, models/litellm_model.py calls os.path.exists(fnm), but `fnm` is never defined, so the documented multi-vLLM serving path would raise NameError at init. By inference, the authors' actual 8B runs used code that differs from the public commit.

datasets-server first-rows returned 10 rows, 4 of them untruncated (rows 0-3, all oauthlib). Across those 4 rows:
- 80 assistant turns, all starting with 'THOUGHT' and all with exactly one ```bash block
- 0 <think>, 0 <tool_call>, 0 tool-role messages
- the edit helper is used in all 4 (row 0 in 3 turns), and each ends with the MINI_SWE_AGENT_FINAL_OUTPUT submit
- the user prompt carries the add_edit_tool.yaml workflow, test-modification ban, edit-tool example and submit text
This is a small sample.

The paper removed only trajectories without a submit-ready patch. It considered excluding test-failing ones, reported a negligible effect, and did not apply that filter. In HF dataset discussion #2, Kwai-Klear org member a Kwai-Klear organisation member and paper author said the trajectories were not validated by unit tests in this version. Requests for success labels (GitHub mini-swe-agent-plus #2; HF discussion #4) are unanswered. The 66k set may therefore include unresolved trajectories.

This corrects the earlier 'unnamed' finding. In HF discussion #2, a Kwai-Klear organisation member and paper author (Kwai-Klear org member, paper author) first said the trajectories came from several top-tier models. Asked for the base LLM, he answered Sonnet 4 (2026-01-23). The paper, dataset card and scaffold README do not name a teacher, and GitHub mini-swe-agent-plus issue #1 asking this is open with 0 comments. Our pin 04d809ce (2026-09-03) is upstream v2.4.6. Its swebench_backticks.yaml:
- requires a ```mswea_bash_command fence
- has step_limit 250, cost_limit 3 and a 60 s timeout
- submits via `git diff > patch.txt` followed by `echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT && cat patch.txt`
- has no edit tool
The default swebench.yaml is tool-calling (parallel_tool_calls: true). So fence, submit protocol, edit tool and step cap all differ from Klear's training and evaluation.

In v2.4.6, action_regex is a LitellmTextbasedModelConfig field (default ```mswea_bash_command), so the fence can be changed in YAML. The submit check in DockerEnvironment._check_finished is hard-coded: first line must be COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT with returncode 0. So the trained MINI_SWE_AGENT_FINAL_OUTPUT submit would not register without a code change, or a prompt asking for the upstream sentinel. That ```bash replies would hit FormatError under the default regex is inferred, not observed. The text model parses only message.content.

ContextRL's repo vendors mini-swe-agent 2.2.8 with a config/benchmarks/swebench_klear.yaml:
- Klear-style THOUGHT + ```bash prompt, but with sed examples and no edit_via_str_replace (0 mentions)
- action_regex overridden to ```bash; submit via MINI_SWE_AGENT_FINAL_OUTPUT && git add -A && git diff --cached
- step_limit 125, temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, no max_tokens
Its docker.py and singularity.py _check_finished are patched to accept both sentinels. scripts/inference_swe_verified.slurm serves vLLM bf16 with --max-model-len 65536 on 500 test instances in singularity sandboxes.

ContextRL (Xu et al., arXiv 2606.17053v1, 15 Jun 2026; six Princeton authors, one UC Davis) Table 1, rows 'Trained from Klear-AgentForge-8B':
- base model: 26.6 Verified / 21.0 Lite
- RL baseline: 28.0 / 21.7
- ContextRL: 30.2 / 24.0
Reference rows: Qwen3-Coder-30B 28.8/22.0, Qwen3-32B 8.40/6.00, Qwen3-14B 8.40/6.00, Qwen3-8B base 5.00/2.70. Scaffold: mini-SWE-agent in SkyRL for both training rollouts and evaluation.

The paper text says Klear-AgentForge-8B, but three sources point to the SFT checkpoint:
- Table 9 lists the agentic base as Klear-AgentForge-8B-SFT.
- The training script run_mini_swe_agentforge8B.sh sets trainer.policy.model.path=/path/to/Klear-AgentForge-8B-SFT.
- The eval config's default model_name is openai/Klear-AgentForge-8B-SFT (overridden at runtime by the served name).
The 26.6 therefore most likely measures Klear-AgentForge-8B-SFT, not the merged fa3d41e9 model; this conclusion is an inference.

Table 7's caps (35 turns, 28,672 max input, 4,096 prompt/response tokens per turn) are training settings. The public eval config differs (125 steps, 64k vLLM context, T=0.6). The paper states no eval temperature, run count or scaffold version, and does not say the public config produced Table 1. The config was committed 2026-06-05, before v1 on 2026-06-15. Comparing 26.6 with 39.4 is confounded by checkpoint, edit tool, step cap and sampling.

These are restatements, not independent runs:
- SWE-MeM Table 1 lists Klear-Agent-8B (Qwen3-8B base, Mini-SWE-agent-plus, 64k) at 39.4, citing the Klear paper.
- SWE-Fuse Table 3 lists Klear-Agent-8B-SFT (Mini-SWE-agent-plus, SFT) at 39.4 and says its baselines come from the original publications or the leaderboard. The SFT label conflicts with the paper's 38.2.

The HF README at fa3d41e9 is only YAML front matter with license: apache-2.0; checked on the raw file, so the earlier uncertainty is resolved. No LICENSE file among siblings. gated=false, private=false. Created 2025-11-12T16:05:49Z, last modified 17:07:15Z. 8,190,735,360 BF16 parameters. 0 discussions.

do_sample true, temperature 0.6, top_k 20, top_p 0.95, eos_token_id [151645, 151643], transformers 4.51.1. These are Qwen3 defaults, probably inherited; they are not the paper's SWE settings, which are unstated.

Qwen3ForCausalLM with 36 layers (all full attention), 32 attention heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, hidden 4096, max_position_embeddings 65536, rope_theta 1e6, no rope_scaling, vocab 151936, bfloat16. This matches the task context.

Without tools the template is plain ChatML: a system block only if messages[0] is a system message, and a generation prompt of exactly '<|im_start|>assistant\n'. There is no enable_thinking variable and no <think> prefill. The <tools>/<tool_call> instructions render only when tools are passed.

The history-reasoning branch reads `{%- if (loop.index0 > ns.last_query_index) and 0 %}`, so it never fires. Past assistant turns are rendered with any text up to </think> removed. The stock Qwen3-8B template (revision b968826d) uses `if loop.index0 > ns.last_query_index` and prefills an empty think block when enable_thinking is false.

eos_token <|im_end|> (151645), pad_token <|endoftext|>, bos_token null, Qwen2Tokenizer, model_max_length 131072 (vs config 65536). <think>/</think> are 151667/151668 and <tool_call>/</tool_call> are 151657/151658.

These readings come from path names only:
- 'swe_6w' suggests about 60k SWE SFT samples, vs 65,994 released rows.
- '4kdat' suggests about 4k RL instances; 'tmpr09' suggests rollout temperature 0.9.
- The tau expert sits under sft_ckpts (continue-training), which suggests an SFT continuation rather than RL. This corrects the task context's 'RL experts for ... tau'.
The README says the 8B was RL-trained from 8B-SFT and then merged.

The paper describes mini-swe-agent-plus as mini-swe-agent plus a string-replacement editing tool. Replacement-style edits make up over 95% of code-modifying tool calls. Rollouts follow ReAct, and the model is derived from Qwen3-8B base.

Sec. 3.3.3: SFT on Deepseek-distill-qwen3-8B (48k-context SFT) collapsed to near zero, with thinking exhausting the 64k limit. The paper never states outright that the released model is non-thinking. Together with think-free SWE data, the template and the sample above, non-thinking is the likely reading, but it is an inference.

SWE SFT data comes only from SWE-smith, filtered to problems with synthesized descriptions: 12,000 problems, distilled with mini-swe-agent-plus into about 66,000 examples. The whole SFT corpus is about 2.4B tokens.

The only SWE decontamination is repository-level: training repositories overlapping the test set were dropped, with no names and no instance, issue or patch check. The one use of 'contamination' concerns code-contest test cases, not SWE.
The paper text contains no SWE-Gym, R2E, rebench, Nebius or SWE-bench-extra. The README names only the 66k dataset.

SWE RL data is described only as SFT samples filtered by an unnamed strong teacher, keeping those solved at least once; no count is given. Reward jumps after about 40 steps, when validation performance starts to decline; the validation set is unnamed. SWE RL ran on 64 H800 GPUs. No SWE RL dataset appears among Kwai-Klear's HF datasets or collections.

llama.cpp 4fea119de30f (2026-09-18, 'ggml-cpu: add F16 input to the FWHT (#27779)') maps LLM_ARCH_QWEN3 to 'qwen3'.
--jinja is enabled by default, and the template comes from GGUF metadata. --reasoning-format defaults to auto: 'none' leaves thoughts in content, 'deepseek' moves them to reasoning_content.

In common/chat.cpp at the pin, the Klear template matches none of the specialized handlers. For example, the Qwen3-Coder handler needs <tool_call> together with <function= and <parameter=, which Klear's template lacks. It therefore goes to the differential autoparser (analyze_template). How that classifies reasoning for this template can only be settled by running it.

evidence.verifier_summary:
I checked every fact by opening its source (raw files at pinned commits, the HF API and dataset-viewer, and arXiv HTML at v1/v2), and re-ran the dataset-viewer counts myself on 2026-09-26. Most claims hold. The corrections and new findings that matter for DTR-REQ-020:

(1) **The one independent score (ContextRL, 26.6) probably measures a different checkpoint.** The paper text names Klear-AgentForge-8B. But its compute table, its public training script (policy path /path/to/Klear-AgentForge-8B-SFT) and the default model name in its eval config all point to Klear-AgentForge-8B-SFT. So 26.6 most likely measures the SFT checkpoint, not the merged fa3d41e9 model we pin.

(2) **ContextRL's public eval setup differs from both Klear's and ours.** Repo xupy2003/ContextAwareRL @0683df93 vendors mini-swe-agent 2.2.8 with a swebench_klear.yaml:
- Klear prompt format, but sed examples instead of the edit tool
- ```bash action_regex and the MINI_SWE_AGENT_FINAL_OUTPUT submit command, with the docker and singularity finish checks patched to accept it
- step_limit 125, T=0.6, top_p 0.95, vLLM max-model-len 65536

The paper never says this exact config produced Table 1, so the '13 points lower' comparison is confounded by checkpoint and scaffold.

(3) **Teacher model named informally.** In HF dataset discussion #2, Kwai-Klear org member and paper author a Kwai-Klear organisation member and paper author said the trajectories came from several top models and, when asked, named Sonnet 4. He also said the data was not unit-test validated in this version. The paper agrees: test-failing trajectories were not excluded. So the 66k SFT set may contain unresolved trajectories.

(4) **Third-party 39.4 citations are not independent.** SWE-MeM and SWE-Fuse only restate the author figure; SWE-Fuse says outright that its baselines come from the original publications.

(5) **Items now verified that earlier researchers left uncertain:**
- The 38.2 SFT score (Table 4).
- An empty model card: the HF card at fa3d41e9 holds only a `license: apache-2.0` line.
- Four fully visible SFT rows, not three: 80 assistant turns, every one THOUGHT + exactly one ```bash block, 0 <think>, 0 <tool_call>, 0 tool-role messages.
- The '39.4 pass@1 single run' label is not supported by the paper.

(6) **Things the earlier reports missed:**
- The public mini-swe-agent-plus vLLM path references an undefined variable (`fnm`), so it would crash as published.
- Its runner supports undocumented local subsets named verified100, verified236 and mysmith.
- The tau merge expert lives under sft_ckpts, so the task context's 'RL experts for tau' is probably wrong.
- In our pin v2.4.6 the fence regex is configurable in YAML, but the submit sentinel is hard-coded in DockerEnvironment.
- At llama.cpp 4fea119 the Klear template matches no specialized chat handler, so the server falls back to its differential autoparser. Behaviour there is unverified without running it.

(7) **Decontamination counts reproduced:**
- 0 rows in the released 66k set for all 12 SWE-bench Verified repositories (plus astroid); positive control oauthlib = 1317.
- 0 rows in public SWE-smith for flask, sympy and the other 10; positive control oauthlib = 940; the OR-syntax control returned 940.
- The reported pandas control (1357) could not be reproduced because the server returned errors.
- SWE-smith's last data upload was 2025-08-25, before Klear's data was built.

Bottom line: 39.4 is a single author-reported figure under the authors' scaffold (200 steps, 64k context, edit tool, matching prompt) with no stated temperature or run count. It must not be carried over to our pinned harness. Comparable evidence for the pinned merged checkpoint under our harness does not exist yet.

Note: the scratchpad files I used (klear_v1_html.txt, ctxrl_html.txt, swesmith_v2_html.txt, klear_firstrows.json, ctxrl_tree.json) are working copies only, under <local scratch directory>
